'''Fayyazuddin'''{{efn|[[Punjabi language|Punjabi]]/{{langx|ur|فياض الدين}}}} (born 10 November 1930) is a Pakistani [[theoretical physicist]] and [[emeritus professor]], specialising in theoretical physics and [[Mathematical Physics|mathematical physics]] at the [[National Centre for Physics]] of [[Quaid-e-Azam University]] in [[Islamabad]].<ref name=NCP/><ref name=ICTP>{{Cite web
  | last = ICTP
  | first =International Centre for Theoretical Physics
  | author-link =International Centre for Theoretical Physics
  | title =News From Associates (scroll down to read this title)
  | work =ICTP News Press
  | publisher =Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics
  | date =1999
  | url =https://portal.ictp.it/pio/words/newsletter/backissues/News_94/dateline.html#anchor386602
  | access-date =9 August 2020 }}</ref> He conducted research in the fields of [[quantum mechanics]], [[particle physics]], and [[Meson|meson physics]]. Fayyazuddin has published numerous papers alongside [[Riazuddin (physicist)|Riazuddin]], including a renowned one on [[Quantum Mechanics]].<ref>[https://trove.nla.gov.au/work/7254371 A modern introduction to particle physics/ Fayyazuddin, Riazuddin] National Library Of Australia (TROVE) website</ref><ref>{{Cite book
  | author1 =Fayyazuddin 
  | author2 = Riazuddin
  | author-link2 =Riazuddin (physicist)
  | title = Quantum mechanics
  | publisher = [[World Scientific]]
  | date = 2000
  | location = Singapore and [[Islamabad]]
  | pages = 1–467
  | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=ot7jq4dTjBEC&q=fayyazuddin 
  | isbn =9971-5-0752-8<!-- Correct hyphenation shown. Hyphenation on the copyright page of the book is incorrect. -->}}
</ref>

==Biography==
Fayyazuddin is the twin brother of [[physicist]] [[Riazuddin (physicist)|Riazuddin]], and a student of [[Abdus Salam]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2016/12/12/salaam-pakistan/ |title=Salaam Pakistan |newspaper=Pakistan Today (newspaper)|author=Abbas Hasan |date=12 December 2016|access-date=8 August 2020}}</ref>

===Education===
He and his twin brother [[Riazuddin (physicist)|Riazuddin]] were born on 10 November 1930 into a [[Punjabis|Punjabi]] family in [[Ludhiana]] where they received their intermediate education. Following the [[partition of India]], the family migrated to [[Lahore]], Pakistan. The two attended [[Punjab University, Lahore|Punjab University]].<ref name=PAS>{{Cite web
 |last         = PAS
 |first        = Pakistan Academy of Sciences
 |author-link   = Pakistan Academy of Sciences
 |title        = Fellows of the Academy (Profile of Fayyazuddin)
 |date         = 20 October 2006
 |url          = http://www.paspk.org/fellow3.htm
 |access-date   =8 August 2020 
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120828172848/http://www.paspk.org/fellow3.htm
 |archive-date = 28 August 2012
 |url-status     = dead
 |df           = dmy-all
}}</ref> Fayyazuddin completed his [[Bachelor of Arts]] with honors in mathematics from Punjab University and subsequently earned  [[Master of Science]] in [[mathematical physics]] under the fellowship of [[Abdus Salam]] in 1953.<ref name=NCP/> His master's degree [[Masters Thesis|dissertation]] ''Methods of Mathematical Physics'' was co-written by Riazuddin. In 1953, he became a [[Master of Philosophy]] in [[particle physics]] with the [[Thesis (academic document)|academic thesis]] ''Energy Loss of Mesons in Crystals'' under the fellowship of [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry]] from the same university.<ref name=NCP/>

After teaching mathematics and physics at Karachi University, Fayyaz traveled to the United Kingdom in 1959. He attended [[Imperial College London]] where [[Abdus Salam]] and Riazuddin served as his teachers. He was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in theoretical [[particle physics]] under the fellowship of Abdus Salam in 1962.<ref name=NCP/><ref>{{Cite web
  | title =Fiazudin
  | work =Mathematics Genealogy Project
  | url =https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=78651
  | format =(html)
  }}</ref> Fayyaz's dissertation was written on the "Preliminary Analysis of Photoproduction of K Mesons in the Mandelstam Representation".<ref>{{Cite journal
  | title =Preliminary Analysis of Photoproduction of K Mesons in the Mandelstam Representation
  | journal =[[Physical Review]]
  | volume =123  | issue =5  | page =1882
  | doi = 10.1103/PhysRev.123.1882
|bibcode = 1961PhRv..123.1882F | year =1961
  | last1 =Fayyazuddin
  }}</ref> Fayyaz then returned to Pakistan and served at the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC).<ref>{{Cite book
  | last =Rehman
  | first = Shahid-Ur-
  | title =Long Road to Chagai: Early Days of PAEC
  | publisher =Print Wise Publications
  | date =1999
  | pages =5
  }}
</ref>

==Academic career==
Fayyazuddin joined the PAEC in 1962 where he worked under the guidance of professor [[Abdus Salam]]<ref name=ICTP/> and continued his research on the [[cosmic ray]] [[mu-meson]]s. He undertook postdoctoral research at the [[Enrico Fermi Institute]] at the [[University of Chicago]] from 1966 to 1968.<ref name=NCP/> At the institute, Fayyaz, [[Faheem Hussain]], Riazuddin, and Peter Rotteli, formed "The Relativity Group", a team of young research scientists in [[special relativity]]. In 1968, when the Institute of Physics was established at the [[University of Islamabad]] (now Quaid-i-Azam University), the scientists eagerly returned to [[Pakistan]]. Fayyazuddin, Hussain, Arif-uz-Zaman, and Sarwar Razmi joined the Institute of Physics.<ref name=NCP>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ncp.edu.pk/pe-fayyazuddin.php |title=Profile of Fayyazuddin |website=National Centre For Physics (NCP) website |date=12 January 2003 |access-date=9 August 2020 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all |archive-date=23 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223015205/http://www.ncp.edu.pk/pe-fayyazuddin.php }}</ref> The institute become an active center for theoretical particle physics research due to their distinguished contribution, and its presence was recognized internationally.<ref name=NCP/>

In 1970, he went to [[Great Britain]], where he attended [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratories]] as an associate research scientist. In 1972, he returned to the Institute of Physics of Quaid-e-Azam University. He joined the Theoretical Physics Group under his brother's guidance and participated in [[Fast neutron calculations]] – a key calculation to develop the weapons.<ref>{{Citation
  | first = Shahidur | last =Rahman
  | title =The Theoretical Physics Group: A Cue from Manhattan Project
  | place =Islamabad
  | publisher =Printwise publications
  | date = 1999
  | pages =78–80
  }}</ref> In 1973, Fayyaz traveled to [[Geneva]], Switzerland where he became a [[Visiting scholar|visiting scientist]] at the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research]] (CERN). In 1977, he returned to Quaid-i-Azam University as a physics professor and subsequently became the [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the Faculty of Natural Sciences. In 1980, he went to [[Saudi Arabia]] where he became a regular professor of physics at the [[King Saud University]] in [[Riyadh]] and a regular professor of physics at the [[Umm al-Qura University|Ummal Qura University]] in [[Mecca]] till 1996. After teaching in Saudi Arabia, he returned to Quaid-i-Azam University in 2005.<ref name=ICTP/> In 2007, Fayyazuddin joined Pakistan's [[National Center for Physics]] as a senior scientist. In 2008, he was awarded ''HEC Distinguished Professor'' award by the [[Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)|Higher Education Commission of Pakistan]].<ref name=ICTP/> In 2000, the [[President of Pakistan]], [[Pervez Musharraf|General Pervez Musharraf]], conferred on him Pakistan's second-highest civilian award [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz]] for his contributions to the field of research in physics and science.<ref name=ICTP/>

==Awards and honors ==
* [[Hilal-i-Imtiaz]] (Crescent of Excellence) Award by the [[Government of Pakistan]] - (2000)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>
* [[Higher Education Commission (Pakistan)|HEC Distinguished Professor Award]] - (2007)
* [[Khwarizmi International Award|Khawarzmi International Award in Physics]] - (2003)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>
* [[Gold Medal]] - [[Pakistan Academy of Sciences]] (1979)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>
* D. Dwyer Bhawani Dass Gold Medal, [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] - (1951)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>

==Fellowships and memberships==
*A fellow of the Third World Academy of Sciences for the Developing World (TWAS)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>
*A research member, National Center for Physics, Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad (1999)<ref name=PAS/>
*An Associate Member at the [[International Center for Theoretical Physics]], [[Trieste]], [[Italy]] (1966–1969, 1972–1980, 1983–1993)<ref name=PAS/>
*An honorary Member of [[American Physical Society]] (1977)<ref name=PAS/><ref name=ICTP/>
*A Life Member of [[Pakistan Physics Society|Pakistan Physical Society]] (1999)<ref name=PAS/>
*A Member, Syndicate, [[Quaid-i-Azam University]] (1975–1977)<ref name=PAS/>
